summary: Yu Yan Pang is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Hong Kong under the supervision of Jing Yin and Cecilia Chan, having also studied under Eric Kvan.

Yu-Chen Tsui is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed master's study at Columbia University supervised by Chün-fang Yü, and later studied under doctoral supervisor Natasha Heller (attested 2018) and traditional teacher Sheng Yen.

Yu-Yin Hsu is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology who earned a Ph.D. from the National University of Singapore (2014–2019) and held a post in the Faculty of East Asian Studies at Ruhr University Bochum in 2022.

Yu-kwan Ng (born 1946) is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who studied at CUHK and under Zongsan Mou before completing a Ph.D. at McMaster University (~1977–1981). He held posts at HKBU (1988) and National Central University (~1996–2011).

Yu-min Lee is a scholar of Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. A student of John C. Huntington, she served as a professor at National Taiwan University (attested 2002) and taught Pei-jung Wu.
Yuan Ren is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology who earned a PhD at McMaster University (attested 1998) under the supervision of Phyllis Granoff.

Yuanxing Guo (1920–1982) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under Gongga Rinpoche. He held posts at the Jinling Scriptural Press and as a researcher at the Research Institute of Chinese Buddhism.

Yuanying (1878–1953) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under masters including Tongzhi and Bazhi Toutuo. He was abbot of Jiedai, Tiantong, and Yongquan temples, founded Yuanming Lengyan School, and served as president of the Buddhist Association of China.

Yudru Tsomu is a scholar of Tibetology and history and archaeology who earned a PhD at Harvard University under doctoral supervisor Leonard van der Kuijp. Her students include Hoong Teik Toh and Cameron David Warner.

Yuen Ren Chao (1892–1982) was a linguist and sinologist who studied at Tsinghua, Cornell (~1910–1914), and Harvard (~1915–1918). He held academic posts at Cornell, Harvard, Tsinghua (~1925–1929), and UC Berkeley (~1947–1963).
Yuexia (1858–1917) was a Buddhist studies figure who founded Huayan University and served as a teacher there.
Yuguang Liu is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at Northwest Minzu University in 2000 and earned a PhD from the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (attested 2005).
Yuhiko Katsuzaki (born 1946) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Taisho University (~1965–1974) and later served as its president (~2011–2015).
Yui Chi Lau (1914–1997) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under Ying-Kuang Chu. He founded the Hong Kong Vajrayana Esoteric Society and taught Shek-Wing Tam.

Yui Suzuki is a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and history and archaeology who earned a doctorate at UCLA under William M. Bodiford, Donald F. McCallum, and Lothar von Falkenhausen, later holding a post at the University of Maryland (attested 2012).

Yuichi Kajiyama (1925–2004) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. He studied at Kyoto University, Nava Nalanda Mahavihara, SOAS, and Vienna, later holding posts at Kyoto University (1956–1988), Bukkyo University (1988–1997), and Soka University (1997–2001).
Yuichi Shionoya (1932–2015) was a scholar in philosophy who studied at Nagoya University (~1949–1953) and Hitotsubashi University (~1953–1958), later holding a post at Nagoya University (~1968–1974).

Yuishin Ito (1931–2023) was a Buddhist studies and history scholar who studied at Bukkyo and Doshisha universities. He taught at Bukkyo University (1961–1997) and held leadership roles at Kyoto Bunkyo Junior College, Kyoto Bunkyo Gakuen, Shōjōke-in, and Chion-in.

Yujiro Motora (1858–1912) was a philosopher who studied at Johns Hopkins University (1885). He held posts at the University of Tokyo (~1888–1912) and Tokyo University of Education (~1890–1900), and taught Daijō Tokiwa.

Yujun Endo (1939–2017) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who taught Ryuichi Abe and Kokan Fujita. He served as associate professor and professor emeritus at Taisho University and advisor at Kawasaki Daishi Research Institute.
